summary: Feed s161_triple is degraded: 3 faults found - 91% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance, 10.8% oversize frames dropped by 1518-byte IDS port, and 17.4% duplicates. IDS is blind to most payloads and losing large frames.

findings.root_cause: 91% of bytes are encrypted (vs 60% IDS tolerance). Traffic is delivered encrypted with no upstream decryption or cleartext mirror, so IDS sees only TLS/encrypted payloads.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature and anomaly detection but cannot inspect encrypted content; ~91% of traffic is opaque, drastically reducing detection coverage and allowing threats to hide in encrypted flows.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext payload to inspect; decrypt at broker or mirror cleartext from TLS-intercept proxy before IDS, respecting privacy/policy, to bring encrypted share below 60%.

findings.root_cause: 347 of 3224 frames (10.8%) exceed IDS 1518-byte MTU, largest 8058 bytes. Likely jumbo frames or encapsulated traffic not normalized for this 1 Gbps IDS port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC silently drops oversized frames, causing ~10.8% traffic loss. IDS misses attacks carried in large frames. Tool needs full payload so broker slicing/trimming to 1518 is not an option.

recommended_fix.why: Normalize MTU at packet broker (reassemble/fragment handling or filter jumbo sources) or upgrade IDS interface to support jumbo frames; do not slice as IDS requires full payload.

findings.root_cause: 562 of 3224 packets (17.4%) are duplicates, well above 5% threshold. Typical cause is aggregating multiple SPAN/mirror sessions or overlapping TAP feeds without broker deduplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: Wastes IDS 1Gbps processing budget, inflates flow/packet counts, skews analytics and can cause false positives or missed correlations while reducing effective detection capacity.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication to deliver single copy of each packet to IDS, eliminating 17% overhead.
